entries.content:
Kate Grinevskaja

Product Manager

Snigdha Jha

Product Manager

As enterprises move AI agents from experimental prototypes into production, data and platform teams are discovering that deploying an agent is only half the battle — you also need to see how it reasons, which data it touches, and what it costs to run. Today, we are announcing expanded AI agent observability and evaluation capabilities across Google Data Cloud, giving you unified visibility into your first-party (1P) data agents in BigQuery and Looker as well as custom third-party (3P) agents built with agent development frameworks such as Agent Development Kit (ADK) or LangGraph.

Putting conversational and autonomous agents into production requires solving three operational challenges: tracing multi-step reasoning while protecting sensitive data, controlling token consumption and query spend, and evaluating answer accuracy before prompt or schema changes reach users. Let’s explore how our new agent observability and evaluation capabilities help you do this.

What's new: Agent observability across Data Cloud

Running agents at scale means you need to see how they perform, what they cost, and what actions they take. We're rolling out a unified telemetry framework across Google's Agentic Data Cloud that works the same way for every agent: Capture telemetry from the agent, land it in BigQuery tables you own, and analyze it wherever your teams already work.

Unified agent observability framework capturing logging telemetry across 1P and 3P agents into BigQuery to surface performance and usage insights across developer and admin tools.

1. Capture telemetry from every first-party and custom agent

  • First-party data agents: Out-of-the-box Conversational Analytics agents emit telemetry automatically with no setup required. Queries routed to BigQuery data agents in Gemini Enterprise through agent-to-agent (A2A) workflows (now GA) send Cloud Monitoring metrics, Cloud Trace spans, and BigQuery conversation logs straight into your agent's project.

  • Custom agents: Agents built with ADK or LangGraph stream the same structured telemetry into BigQuery through single-line SDK instrumentation.

2. Land telemetry in one governed home in BigQuery

  • Conversation logging in BigQuery (GA): Managed 1P conversation logging writes to BigQuery tables you own, so you can inspect Conversational Analytics traces, including prompts and responses, directly in your data warehouse.

  • Governed by default: The Conversational Analytics API, now GA, includes always-on admin audit logs and optional data-read audit logs in Cloud Audit Logs, and supports VPC Service Controls, customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK), and regional and multi-regional data residency.

3. Analyze with dashboards wherever your teams work

  • In BigQuery (GA): Agent monitoring provides prebuilt dashboards in BigQuery Studio to track usage, active sessions, top knowledge sources, and latency across BigQuery Conversational Analytics agents.

BigQuery Conversational Analytics dashboard in BigQuery Studio, giving admins visibility into usage, active sessions, top knowledge sources, and latency.

  • In Looker (GA): System Activity dashboards for Conversational Analytics, now GA in Looker (Google Cloud core) and Looker (original), track engagement and token usage, while user ratings and query review in the Responses & feedback tab are in preview.

Looker Conversational Analytics dashboard in System Activity, giving admins visibility into usage, token consumption, and user feedback.

  • Build your own: Create interactive reports with the open-source Data Studio template or deploy the ready-made Looker Block for Agent Analytics for real-time custom agent monitoring.

Custom Data Studio dashboard built on BigQuery Agent Analytics logs to track token consumption, latency, and user engagement.

Looker Block dashboard built on BigQuery Agent Analytics telemetry to monitor session volumes, tool execution latency, and token cost distribution.

Tracing agent reasoning and protecting privacy

Enterprise observability requires balancing diagnostic telemetry with strict data privacy boundaries. Because tracking features involve ingestion and storage costs, Google Data Cloud separates operational telemetry from conversation content so admins and agent owners can govern each layer independently.

At the project or organization level, admins can enable Cloud Monitoring (aggregate metrics such as request volume, latency, and token usage) and Cloud Trace (step-by-step spans for each request) across their environment, using Cloud Trace observability scopes to consolidate telemetry across multiple agent projects. To protect sensitive data, these operational metrics and sanitized first-party trace spans exclude customer core content (such as user prompts, model responses, internal thoughts, and generated SQL).

When you need deeper transcript auditing, agent owners and editors can opt in to conversation logging on a per-agent basis:

  • Governed conversation logging in BigQuery: When enabled, a Google-managed service agent streams user prompts, responses, and turn-level telemetry into a customer-owned BigQuery table (

    agent_events
    ) via the BigQuery Storage Write API, inheriting your dataset's IAM permissions, CMEK, and VPC Service Controls. Built-in privacy guardrails enforce a fail-closed check before each turn — skipping logging whenever a knowledge source uses row-level security, column-level policy tags, or dynamic data masking — while fail-open execution keeps your users' chat sessions uninterrupted if a logging error occurs.

  • Full trace trees for custom 3P agents: While 1P conversation logging intentionally strips low-level tool arguments and internal SQL, developers building custom agents on ADK or LangGraph can instrument their code with the open-source ADK plugin (

    BigQueryAgentAnalyticsPlugin
    ). With a single-line setup, the SDK streams full tool-invocation execution trees, time-series telemetry, and multimodal payloads straight into BigQuery.

  • In-warehouse root cause and drift analysis: Because conversation logs land natively in your 

    agent_events
    table, you don't need separate export pipelines to diagnose failures. You can run BigQuery AI functions (such as 
    AI.GENERATE
    to summarize error patterns and 
    AI.EMBED
    with 
    VECTOR_SEARCH
    to cluster recurring issues) or use the open-source 
    bigquery-agent-analytics
    Python SDK and Colab starter notebook for post-hoc semantic drift clustering and LLM-as-a-judge sentiment analysis.

Controlling token costs with FinOps guardrails

As agent adoption grows, FinOps and platform teams need clear visibility into consumption alongside active controls to prevent runaway spend. With promotional trial pricing currently available for Conversational Analytics, now is a good time to establish baseline usage and cost guardrails:

  • Granular token and latency tracking: In BigQuery conversation logs, each turn records input, output, thought, cached, and total token counts alongside total turn latency, while Looker System Activity reports estimated input and output tokens across your business intelligence (BI) workloads.

  • Turnkey observability dashboards: You can track projected token usage and engagement in the BigQuery Studio Monitoring tab and native Looker System Activity dashboards, or query 

    agent_events
    log data via BigQuery SQL using the open-source seven-page Data Studio report template and self-hosted Streamlit app in the BigQuery Agent Analytics GitHub repository.

  • Active query and token spend caps: To prevent unexpected charges before they happen, you can configure per-query BigQuery byte scan caps (

    big_query_max_billed_bytes
    ) on your agent, which use dry-run estimates to block oversized queries without incurring on-demand scan charges. For BigQuery and the Conversational Analytics API, you can also enforce daily input and output token quotas (in preview) per project, user, or agent in the Google Cloud console and 
    gcloud
    CLI.

Evaluating and benchmarking your AI agents

Runtime observability works alongside systematic evaluation. While logs and traces tell you how an agent behaved in production, evaluation benchmarks verify whether updates to your prompts, models, or data schemas improve SQL accuracy and answer quality before users experience a regression:

  • Benchmarking with Prism: Our open-source evaluation tool, Prism, lets you test Conversational Analytics agents grounded in BigQuery tables or Looker Explores via the Conversational Analytics API using reusable test suites, regex assertions, and multi-region agent discovery (deployed behind an access layer such as Cloud IAP).

  • Unified evaluation and production analytics: Prism can stream completed evaluation runs directly into day-partitioned BigQuery tables in your project, placing your pre-deployment benchmark scores right alongside your production 

    agent_events
    logs for side-by-side analysis in BigQuery and Looker.

  • Native BigQuery evaluations: First-party agent evaluations in BigQuery (built on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform evaluation service with bring-your-own-service-account support) are available in preview via API and a guided Colab notebook.

Getting started

Ready to bring visibility, governance, and cost control to your AI agents? Here is how to get started in three steps:

  • Enable first-party agent observability. Turn on Cloud Monitoring and Cloud Trace in your project and opt in to per-agent conversation logging using the BigQuery agent monitoring guide, and track BI token consumption with the Looker Conversational Analytics overview and Looker System Activity documentation.

  • Instrument custom agents and deploy analytics dashboards. Add the BigQuery Agent Analytics SDK to your ADK or LangGraph agents, launch the open-source Data Studio report template or Streamlit app, and explore in-warehouse log analysis with the Colab starter notebook.

  • Benchmark your agents and set cost guardrails. Run automated accuracy suites with Prism, and configure BigQuery byte scan caps and daily token quotas via Manage BigQuery costs for agents.

entries.content:
Megan Gawlik

Product Manager, HPC

Annie Ma-Weaver

Group Product Manager, HPC

Computational scientists and HPC engineers have always been among the earliest adopters of new computing paradigms, and agents are no exception. Today, research and engineering teams use AI models and agents for things such as ingesting dense scientific literature, optimizing code, and autonomously steering simulations.

Yet moving from an agent that suggests code optimizations to an agentic system that reliably architects, provisions, and optimizes production HPC workloads at scale takes more than a general-purpose reasoning model. Without deep infrastructure and domain context, an unguided agent can still pair incompatible storage tiers with compute-optimized VMs, overlook placement policies, or stall when diagnosing a multi-node MPI fabric error.

That challenge led our team to ask a simple question: What if we could package our deep HPC and scientific expertise into reusable agent skills, turning complex setup and optimization into guided workflows?

At SC26, we are showing how Google Cloud brings agentic HPC to life with reusable skills that teach agents how to build and run HPC workloads. In addition, we’re also demonstrating evolutionary agents that optimize your algorithms at cloud scale, and purpose-built supercomputing infrastructure designed for where HPC meets AI.

Teaching agents to speak HPC: From blueprints to skills

Organizations rely on Cluster Toolkit to deploy repeatable, production-ready HPC environments on Google Cloud through declarative YAML blueprints. Now we are expanding these capabilities by pairing Cluster Toolkit with composable agent skills with self-describing, deterministic tools, validated through automated, end-to-end testing and available for download from the Google Skills and DeepMind Science Skills repositories. Together, this delivers:

  • Infrastructure skills that validate before they deploy: When you ask an agent to stand up a cluster, the skill directs it to first audit your compute and storage quotas, run rapid canary checks for regional capacity, match your workload to a validated Cluster Toolkit blueprint, and wait for human approval, all before running the gcluster deploy command.

  • Workload-specific skills that know the science: After your cluster is live, domain skills connected to Google Skills and DeepMind Science Skills guide the agent through things like configuring OpenFOAM and Siemens STAR-CCM+ fluid dynamics runs, tuning GROMACS and AlphaFold 3 life-sciences pipelines, or launching Devito and Open Porous Media (OPM) subsurface simulations with browser-based 3D visualization.

  • Built-in governance and Day-2 diagnostics: Agents operate inside strict IAM, Kueue quota, and budget guardrails, with full provenance in Cloud Logging and structured troubleshooting skills (gke-kueue-debugging) to resolve stuck queues or node drains automatically.

Scaling from local prototype to breakthrough code

Configuring and running existing solvers is only part of the discovery loop. Across financial services, electronic design automation (EDA), manufacturing, logistics, pharmaceuticals, and AI training, competitive advantage comes from having the fastest underlying code and algorithms. Historically, squeezing out performance gains required scarce optimization specialists and costly brute-force compute.

Developed by Google DeepMind, AlphaEvolve changes the equation by using a Gemini-powered evolutionary loop to iteratively mutate, benchmark, and optimize code and 3D engineering parameters against target metrics. The AlphaEvolve on Cloud Batch solution,  streamlines the process of moving from a seed algorithm on a laptop to massive parallel experimentation. With Batch, you get:

  • Automated parallel evaluation: A single gcluster blueprint provisions the AlphaEvolve controller environment and uses Batch to fan out hundreds of candidate evaluations concurrently across single-VM sandboxes or multi-node MPI task groups.

  • Interactive control from your preferred surface: Researchers can steer evolutionary experiments and inspect candidate lineage through hosted Python notebooks, or integrate optimization runs directly into their existing CLI workloads and agent-driven development tools.

  • Evaluation at production scale: Evolving an algorithm on a single node with slow networking risks producing code that only performs well at small scale. By evaluating candidates across Google Cloud compute instances with Cloud RDMA and Google Cloud Managed Lustre — and using Spot VMs or Dynamic Workload Scheduler (DWS) to balance cost against turnaround time — you discover algorithms tuned for real supercomputing fabrics, permanently lowering the compute cost of every future production run.

Supercomputing infrastructure under the hood

An autonomous workflow is only as capable as the infrastructure beneath it. As agentic pipelines pivot dynamically between memory-bandwidth-bound physics solvers, domain foundation models (like AlphaFold 3, AlphaGenome, and WeatherNext), and large-scale AI training, Google Cloud provides a unified hardware and orchestration fabric managed by Cluster Director that offers:

  • Tightly coupled HPC and scale-out compute: Run classic MPI simulations on H4D instances powered by 5th Gen AMD EPYC processors and Cloud RDMA, including 3 TB high-memory shapes built for large EDA and engineering models. Alternatively, you can maximize performance-per-watt on Arm-based C4A instances powered by Google Axion.

  • Next-generation GPU acceleration: Run coupled physics-AI pipelines and multi-node GPU simulations on A4 and A4X instances (NVIDIA Blackwell B200 and GB200 NVL72), scale frontier AI training and reasoning on newly available A5X bare metal instances built on the NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, and use G4 instances with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs to accelerate CAE, CFD, and 3D visualization while reducing per-core software licensing costs.

  • 8th gen TPUs for the agentic era: Deploy 8th generation TPUs, featuring TPU 8t for large-scale pre-training, reinforcement learning, and accelerated mathematical modeling and simulation (ModSim), alongside TPU 8i for high-throughput, low-latency reasoning and agentic inference. Additionally, Batch now supports running jobs on single-host TPU slices, providing flexible provisioning options for accelerated HPC and AI/ML workloads.

  • Sub-millisecond parallel storage: Reduce data bottlenecks between simulation and AI stages with Google Cloud Managed Lustre, delivering up to 10 TB/s of read throughput, GPUDirect Storage over RDMA, and an 80 PB Dynamic Tier with Cloud Storage Mirroring. For even more performance, you can pair it with Cloud Storage FUSE local SSD caching.

Experience it live at SC26 in Chicago

Agentic HPC is not about turning unguided models loose on a terminal. This shift is about combining the reasoning power of Gemini with the codified engineering of Cluster Toolkit skills, evolutionary optimization on Batch, and purpose-built supercomputing hardware — so your teams spend their time on discovery rather than infrastructure plumbing.

Visiting SC26 (November 15–20)? Stop by Booth #3418 at McCormick Place West for live demos of Antigravity for HPC, the HPC Prompt Playground, and AlphaEvolve for HPC, and join us at our Advanced Computing Community Half-Day Workshop and Agentic and Hybrid HPC Birds of a Feather (BoF) session.

To start building today, explore the Google Cloud Cluster Toolkit and Google Cloud HPC solutions. To access and implement these agentic workflows, download the validated templates from the Google Skills and DeepMind Science Skills repositories.

entries.content:
Jelson A. Cordeiro

Solutions & Cloud Architect, Copel

Nick Orlove

Product Manager, BigQuery

Bridging the gap between analytical systems (OLAP) and transactional databases (OLTP) is notoriously complex. Synchronizing data between the two systems, often called Reverse ETL (Extract, Transform, Load), traditionally requires heavy middleware, staging buckets, and complex orchestration, especially at enterprise scale.

We’re announcing the general availability (GA) of BigQuery exports to AlloyDB, allowing data engineering teams to use a single, declarative SQL statement to export data from BigQuery to AlloyDB. This approach completely removes the need for complex ETL middleware.

To demonstrate the benefits of this feature, we are sharing how Copel, a Brazilian electric power provider, eliminated a massive orchestration bottleneck and scaled their smart meter telemetry by migrating to high-performance, built-in Reverse ETL.

The challenge of scaling smart meter telemetry

At Copel, managing telemetry data from millions of smart electricity meters is a mission-critical operation. This data is streamed continuously and consolidated in an analytical Gold layer in BigQuery. However, to power Copel's "Systems of Action" — low-latency customer support dashboards, mobile applications, and operational billing systems — this rich dataset must be constantly synced back into its high-performance transactional database, AlloyDB for PostgreSQL.

Until recently, Copel orchestrated this Reverse ETL architecture with a complex DAG in Google’s Managed Service for Apache Airflow. However, there were multiple brittle, intermediate stages in the process of enriching and exporting hundreds of millions of records from BigQuery to AlloyDB:

Figure 1: Copel’s legacy multi-stage architecture requiring Cloud Storage file dumps and sequential gCloud scripts.

  • BigQuery ran enrichment and extraction queries, dumping SQL results into dozens of fragmented CSV files inside a Google Cloud Storage bucket.

  • Apache Airflow executed SQL to create temp tables in AlloyDB to prevent write locking or data corruption for production tables.

  • Sequential gCloud scripts combed through the Cloud Storage CSVs to load data into a respective AlloyDB cluster and shards.

  • Finally, a SQL transaction block safely dropped the production table and renamed the temporary table to production.

To run this legacy architecture, Copel’s team needed to maintain the pipeline, carefully manage file staging, perform complex IAM impersonation across multiple services, and constantly monitor end-to-end system health.

The breakthrough: Built-in Reverse ETL

With BigQuery's 

EXPORT DATA
to AlloyDB, Copel was able to replace this entire multi-step pipeline infrastructure with a single, elegant SQL statement.

Now, BigQuery exports communicate directly with AlloyDB instances over highly optimized, parallelized connections — no staging files in Cloud Storage, gCloud scripts, or managing temporary tables required!

Figure 2: New architecture showing direct parallel Reverse ETL connection between BigQuery and AlloyDB.

Here is how simple the new Reverse ETL process looks in code:

The resulting BigQuery values map perfectly to AlloyDB's columns during the export, leaving the nested structures fully queryable and indexable on the PostgreSQL side.

Evaluating performance and scalability

To validate this new architecture, Copel executed two large-scale Reverse ETL benchmarks: comparing the performance and scalability of a smaller incremental Reverse ETL export against a much larger full-table Reverse ETL export.

The performance results exceeded all initial expectations:

Pro-tip on ingestion: Sustaining an export throughput of ~4.2 million rows/minute on complex 

JSONB
telemetry fields is an outstanding technical achievement. It highlights the low-level optimizations between BigQuery's distributed processing engine and AlloyDB's advanced storage layer.

Key takeaways and benefits

By adopting this declarative SQL approach, Copel successfully deleted dozens of lines of complex scripting and custom error-handling blocks. Their Airflow DAG now contains a single, simplified 

BigQueryInsertJobOperator
task that executes the export query.

This built-in approach unlocks several core business benefits:

  • Direct cost reduction: By bypassing Cloud Storage entirely, there are no staging storage costs and associated API read/write operation fees.

  • Enhanced data security: Data moves directly from BigQuery to AlloyDB inside Google's secure internal network without ever being dumped into readable CSV files.

  • Near-zero maintenance: Pipeline errors are now contained within a single SQL statement, making troubleshooting and logging drastically simpler.

  • Massive distributed writing: The direct export achieved write speeds exceeding 4 million records per minute by leveraging BigQuery's massive parallelism combined with AlloyDB's optimized PostgreSQL write performance.

Now, rather than spending valuable engineering hours monitoring pipeline failures and intermediate storage buffers, data engineering teams can focus on what matters: delivering smart analytics and premium experiences to customers.

Get started today: Modernize your Reverse ETL

Now that BigQuery exports to AlloyDB are generally available, there has never been a better time to simplify your data architecture. If your team is struggling with complex, multi-stage pipelines to push BigQuery data into downstream OLTP databases, we invite you to try built-in export functionality for AlloyDB, Bigtable, Spanner, or Pub/Sub today.

Want to know the latest from Google Cloud? Find it here in one handy location. Check back regularly for our newest updates, announcements, resources, events, learning opportunities, and more.

Tip: Not sure where to find what you’re looking for on the Google Cloud blog? Start here: Google Cloud blog 101: Full list of topics, links, and resources.

Nov 9 - Nov 13

  • More frontier model choice on Google Cloud: Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 and Meta’s Muse model series.

Developers now have even more flexibility to build, deploy, and scale with the right model for every workload on Google Cloud. Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 is now generally available in the Model Garden, bringing frontier intelligence to complex coding, scientific research, and multi-agent orchestration. Plus, Meta’s newest models—Muse Spark 1.3, Muse Wonder, and the efficient Muse Ember—are now available in public preview, giving teams seamless access to both proprietary and open-weight capabilities with enterprise-grade security.

Explore the models in the model garden today.

  • Next-Generation SecOps: SentinelOne and Google Cloud

    Google Cloud and SentinelOne joined forces to solve the threat scaling challenge with a fundamentally re-architected integration. As a Google Unified Security (GUS) Recommended endpoint detection and response (EDR) partner, SentinelOne pairs Google Security Operations through an optimized direct integration and streamlined data schemas, delivering essential endpoint telemetry visibility to SecOps detection and agentic SOC pipelines while significantly reducing the total cost of ownership of the integration.

    Read more
  • Layered LLM guardrails on Apigee: Static rules, Model Armor, and NeMo Guardrails 

    No single LLM guardrail catches every threat. A new technical guide and demo showcase how to use Apigee as an AI gateway to stack three complementary layers—deterministic static rules, semantic Google Cloud Model Armor filters, and flexible business logic via NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails. Together, they successfully intercepted 100% of benchmarked OWASP-mapped attacks without blocking safe prompts, running cheapest first to optimize performance and reduce token costs.

    Read the full guide
  • Scale Gemma 3 reinforcement learning on GKE with NVIDIA NeMo RL, Custom ComputeClasses, and 8-NIC RDMA

    Learn how to run distributed Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) post-training for Gemma 3 on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). This end-to-end blueprint pairs GKE Custom ComputeClasses (with DWS Flex-Start and Spot fallback) and 8-NIC RoCE RDMA networking with NVIDIA NeMo RL and vLLM V1 to improve Gemma 3 mathematical reasoning accuracy.

    Read the technical guide
  • Securely connect internal Cloud Run MCP servers to Gemini Enterprise

    Learn how to connect Gemini Enterprise privately to internal StreamableHTTP Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers on Cloud Run using Egress Agent Gateway, Private Service Connect (PSC), FQDN-scoped Private Cloud DNS for Shared VPCs, and dual-header OAuth 2.0 + IAM authentication. Read thetechnical guide on Google Developer Forums and explore the reference implementation on GitHub.
  • Building an adaptive AI gateway with Apigee for stateful multi-agent workloads

    Multi-agent workloads often suffer from compounding context bloat, retry loops, and cross-agent state bleed.. Learn how to use Apigee as a model-agnostic, stateful multi-agent control plane for Google ADK and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform workloads. By enforcing turn-0 pre-warmed caching, in-flight trace compaction, tool loop recovery, and dynamic model tiering between Gemini Flash and Frontier models, teams can achieve up to 80% net FinOps cost savings.

    Read the full article to explore reference architectures and benchmark data.
  • Anthropic’s exponential growth on Pub/Sub

    Discover how Anthropic, creators of the Claude AI models, uses Google Cloud Pub/Sub to power their cross-cloud telemetry and billing ingestion pipeline. Facing highly variable traffic and strict security mandates, Anthropic needed a secure, serverless messaging queue with zero manual partition management. By leveraging Pub/Sub with Private Service Connect, they built a highly efficient, zero-ETL architecture capable of seamlessly handling over 1 million events per second and 500 billion daily rows. Go behind the scenes in thiscase study to learn how Anthropic reduced consumer latency by 88% and achieved sub-second end-to-end event delivery.
  • On-demand webinar: Architecting AI workloads with Pub/Sub

    Data engineering in the AI era demands fundamentally different infrastructure. Whether you're training a custom foundation model or deploying autonomous agents, you need a messaging backbone that handles bursty traffic with enterprise security and zero operational overhead. Dive into Pub/Sub’s capabilities for the AI era, reference architectures & best practices for emerging AI applications, and how Anthropic powers their telemetry pipelines with Pub/Sub inthis free on-demand webinar.

Nov 2 - Nov 6

  • Security for AI workloads with Model Armor

    Securing generative AI applications requires robust runtime protection against prompt injection and malicious inputs. Join Nicola Cardace on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 5:00 PM CET for a Community TechTalk exploring how to safeguard enterprise AI workloads using Model Armor. Discover practical patterns for implementing active model defense across your LLM endpoints.

    Register for the November 19 Community TechTalk

  • A5X accelerated by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 is now Generally Available

    Get the most out of A5X instances with Google Cloud’s AI Hypercomputer. Bringing together compute, storage, networking, and software co-designed as a single system. 

    Read more

Oct 26 - Oct 30

  • Simplify PostgreSQL Monitoring with the New AlloyDB Omni Web UI

    The newly released AlloyDB Omni Web UI delivers a centralized, graphical dashboard that simplifies the management of self-managed PostgreSQL workloads across hybrid, multi-cloud, and air-gapped environments. This browser-based console provides database administrators with deep, real-time insights into cluster health, hardware utilization, and active database connections. It also features built-in query diagnostics and performance tracking for AlloyDB’s columnar engine, enabling quick troubleshooting of bottlenecks without manual terminal commands. To learn more about setting up this monitoring interface, read the fullAlloyDB Omni Web UI Blog Post.
  • Leveraging "Antigravity" to architect high performance semantic model routers in Apigee

    Semantic model routing replaces rigid static paths with a lightweight helper model to dynamically classify and dispatch intent-driven LLM traffic. Join Saravanakumar Rajagopal on Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 5:00 PM CET for a Community TechTalk exploring how to leverage Antigravity and skills to architect these intelligent multi-provider routing patterns natively inside Apigee. Discover how to optimize your AI infrastructure and enhance flexibility at scale.

    Register for the November 12 Community TechTalk

Oct 19 - Oct 23

  • From prompt to production: End-to-end AI workflows in Apigee

    Deploying an enterprise AI gateway does not require deep API or machine learning expertise. Using declarative workflows in Apigee, teams can spin up a fully governed LLM gateway in minutes using a few environment variables. Join Luis Cuellar on Thursday, October 29, 2026 for a Community TechTalk exploring end-to-end AI workflows. Discover how to layer essential defenses—including Model Armor for prompt protection, Cloud Data Loss Prevention (Cloud DLP) for sensitive data redaction, rate limiting, and response caching—before routing autonomous agent interactions through your gateway filters.

    Register for the October 29 Community TechTalk
  • Zero Standing Privileges with PAM: On-Demand Temporary Access for Humans and AI Agents

    AI agents now hand work off to other agents, risking stacked privileges and overpermissioning. Because agents plan their actions on the fly, permanent admin access means one hallucination can cascade into production. Join us on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, at 8:30 AM PST to see how Google CloudPrivileged Access Manager (PAM) brings Zero Standing Privileges to AI delegation, putting humans in command with cloud-native control that doesn't slow developers down.

    Register for the November 18 webinar

    Native streaming support is now in Public Preview for API Gateway, enabling you to run real-time and AI workloads behind your existing gateway. You can now route Server-Sent Events (SSE), WebSockets, gRPC, and chunked transfer encoding without modifying your API spec or managing a split estate. This update also strengthens integration with the Gemini platform, allowing you to stream responses from Gemini, Claude, and OpenAI gpt-oss models seamlessly while maintaining consistent authentication, rate limiting, and observability.

    Read the blog to get started

Oct 12 - Oct 16

  • AI tokenomics in action: Enforcing tiered token budgets with Apigee

    Scaling artificial intelligence across an enterprise requires clear token governance to keep LLM spend predictable across departments. Join Tarun Abraham on Thursday, November 5, 2026 for a Community TechTalk on AI tokenomics. Discover how to use Apigee to enforce isolated, tiered token budgets and model access for each team—such as assigning Engineering a dedicated budget for Gemini Pro while covering mixed usage for Marketing—without changing application code. Attendees will also gain access to a sample codebase featuring a reusable Shared Flow.

    Register for the November 5 Community TechTalk

Sept 28 - Oct 2

  • Claude Sonnet 5.5 is now available on Google Cloud. Built for focused coding and knowledge work, it delivers stronger performance for feature development, and creating presentation-ready documents, while offering more intelligence with a lower cost per task for most work at faster speed.

    Deploy Sonnet 5.5 directly from Model Garden with Google Cloud’s enterprise security, scale, and governance built in. Try it now.

  • Mastering Storage Management with Storage Intelligence

    In our new blog, explore practical strategies to modernize storage operations using Storage Intelligence Advisor and enhanced Batch Operations. See how customers like Shipt and Palo Alto Networks are using these features to manage their estates at scale. Today, Storage Intelligence is used by 25 of the top 50 GCS customers. 2 in 3 customers have Storage Intelligence enabled for over 90% of their storage footprint.

    Explore best practices on our blog
  • Cut Gen AI costs by 70% with Apigee X dynamic routing

    Generative AI deployments face a harsh cost-performance trade-off: static model selection either wastes budget or compromises quality. Discover how to build an Intelligent AI Gateway using Apigee X to dynamically evaluate prompt complexity in real-time. This new blueprint automatically routes simple queries to lightweight models (like Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite) and complex reasoning tasks to advanced models (like Gemini 3.7 Flash), achieving over 70% cost savings without sacrificing output quality.

    Read the guide to optimize your Gen AI architecture

entries.content:
Ashley Moulton

Healthcare Lead, Chrome Enterprise Ecosystem, Google

Special offer for healthcare organizations

Chrome Enterprise Premium offers enhanced protections for patient data.

Learn more

Healthcare is adopting AI quickly, and it's moving beyond chat. Clinical teams are starting to use AI agents that draft documentation, summarize charts, navigate web apps, and complete multi-step tasks on a clinician's behalf. Many of these agents work in the same place—the browser. As electronic health records (EHRs) and clinical apps move to the web, the browser is where clinicians, applications, patient data, and AI services meet. When clinicians or agents act inside a session, security teams need clear control over what they can access.

Healthcare systems frequently adopt a multi-vendor AI strategy, a flexibility that should be fully supported. Whether clinicians are using Gemini™ or an array of other web-based AI tools and extensions, Chrome Enterprise Premium secures data across the board to:

  • Guard sensitive data: Advanced DLP controls restrict unauthorized copying and pasting, form submission, printing, and screen capture of sensitive data—preventing patient data from leaking into unapproved AI prompts or browser extensions.
  • Maintain full operational visibility: Granular reporting and visibility into browser activity, extension usage, and data transfers help security teams uncover shadow AI and maintain internal oversight.
  • Govern extensions and web AIs consistently: Security policies and extension controls apply directly at the browser layer, so IT teams can manage permissions, block risky extensions, and enforce guardrails across every AI service without needing a separate harness for each tool.

Since we introduced new healthcare integrations in May, Chrome Enterprise has continued to invest in the healthcare ecosystem. Today we're sharing the next set of milestones that bring Chrome Enterprise to more clinical endpoints.

Chrome Enterprise is now compatible with IGEL OS™

As healthcare organizations accelerate the adoption of web-based clinical applications and AI-powered workflows, securing both the browser and the endpoint has become increasingly important. To address this, Chrome Enterprise is now compatible with the IGEL Adaptive Secure Endpoint Platform™ and will soon be available in the IGEL App Portal,® allowing healthcare IT teams to easily deploy and manage the browser across IGEL OS™ endpoints, including shared workstations, nursing stations, and clinical carts.

This collaboration combines Google's enterprise-grade browser management and security capabilities with the IGEL Adaptive Secure Endpoint Platform,™ providing an immutable, trusted, and centrally governed endpoint foundation designed to reduce the attack surface and simplify IT operations. Through the IGEL App Portal® and IGEL Universal Management Suite™ (UMS™), organizations can streamline application deployment and endpoint governance, while the Google Admin console provides centralized browser policy and extension management.

Native browsing for flexible clinical endpoints with Citrix® UniconOS

Through our expanded collaboration with Citrix, healthcare systems can now run Chrome Enterprise natively on Citrix UniconOS endpoints. Clinicians get a fast, familiar experience on any device, while IT gains another flexible option for adding secure access and data protections across their clinical environments.

Expanding collaboration with Omnissa® for enhanced device trust

Many healthcare organizations use Omnissa Workspace ONE® and Omnissa Horizon® to manage, secure and deliver critical clinical applications. We're expanding our collaboration with Omnissa to bring zero-trust security and device posture assessment to healthcare environments. Building on May's integration, organizations can verify device health before clinicians reach critical applications.

Optimizing Epic® Workflows at the point of care

Beyond endpoint expansion, we are introducing new Chrome Enterprise capabilities that streamline clinic workflows, including support for silent printing and PDF updates for Epic® Hyperspace® for the web. This allows clinicians to route essential orders and wristbands directly to authorized printers, while native PDF rendering keeps protected health information strictly isolated within the active, managed session.

Scaling clinical technology with confidence

Together, these updates give IT and security teams the confidence to say yes to modern clinical technology, supporting the patient care experience—without giving up critical protections and control. As healthcare organizations continue deploying enterprise AI solutions like Gemini or managing a fast-growing ecosystem of third-party AI web apps and browser extensions, Chrome Enterprise provides the unified security, Data Loss Prevention (DLP), and governance layer needed to empower care teams with confidence.

To get started, explore Chrome Enterprise in the IGEL Marketplace, see how our latest updates support your Epic® and clinical workflows or visit our website or contact us today.

entries.content:
Bharath Sivaraman

Senior Product Manager

Even as sophisticated, new zero-day exploits continue to emerge, most cybersecurity incidents still start from the same common sources: an attacker locating and exploiting a fundamental, easily preventable cloud misconfiguration.

Organization Policy Service can help you secure resource configurations and set up security guardrails across your Google Cloud resource hierarchy. Using a catalog of over 100 predefined policies for many common cloud governance needs, as well as Custom Organization Policy, you can more easily set up boundaries with granular control over resources.

To help platform and security teams author, audit, and scale guardrails with greater speed and simplicity, we are introducing the general availability of our Organization Policy Model Context Protocol (MCP) server and natural-language constraint authoring powered by Gemini.

Managing Organization Policy with agents

Rather than forcing administrators to manually parse complex hierarchy chains, the Organization Policy MCP server offers tools that allow autonomous agents and pipelines to interact directly with Organization Policy. 

Using the Organization Policy MCP server, agents can assist administrators with posture audits, drift detection, and exemption management. Key capabilities include:

  • Constraint discovery: Tools like 'ListConstraints' and 'GetCustomConstraint' allow agents to understand the specific guardrails that apply to a project, folder, or organization.

  • Policy evaluation: The 'GetEffectivePolicy' tool calculates the effective policy after considering hierarchy inheritance and tag-based conditions. You can use this to verify if a configuration change will be compliant.

  • Manage policy: 'CreatePolicy' and 'CreateCustomConstraint' allow platform teams to manage guardrails via conversational workflows.

For example, you can combine your preferred coding agent with the Organization Policy MCP tools to create a custom dashboard to visualize the constraints applied to an organization and identify the folders and projects in the organization that have been exempted from the policy. You can also build custom agents and skills to streamline managing Organization Policy.

Figure 1: Custom dashboard created with Organization Policy MCP tools displaying enforced constraints

Figure 2: Visualize enforced constraints and identify exemptions with Organization Policy MCP tools.

Simplifying custom constraint authoring with Gemini

While the Organization Policy constraint catalog provides built-in managed constraints for common use cases, each organization has its own unique architectural standards. Custom Organization Policy enables customers to express these standards as a custom constraint and enforce them across supported services. 

Traditionally, administrators would write these rules in common expression language (CEL), which required a sharp understanding of Google Cloud resource schemas. Today, administrators can author custom Organization Policy in natural language through a Gemini prompt.

For example, you can prompt Gemini to require the use of agent-identity in Agent Runtime, to require that all agents deployed to Agent Runtime use an approved Agent Gateway, and to prevent users from disabling auto-upgrades on GKE, and refine custom constraints conversationally. 

To help ensure safe deployments, Gemini can also generate compliant and non-compliant test resource configurations that can help you test policy and validate in dry-run mode before enforcing the constraint.

Figure 3: Define custom constraints with a natural language prompt using Gemini

For targeted examples, the sample custom constraints library from Google Cloud Professional Services features pre-authored custom constraint samples based on CIS and PCI standards. Custom constraints are supported on a wide range of Google Cloud services including core AI and compute services including Agent Runtime, Agent Search, and Agent Studio on Gemini platform, Cloud Run, and Google Kubernetes Engine. 

Build faster, with confidence

Organization Policy provides proactive cloud governance of resource configurations on Google Cloud. It lets administrators enforce critical security guardrails so engineering teams can build and deploy quickly and securely.

With a growing catalog of built-in guardrails, autonomous tools for administrators, and the ability to tailor custom constraints across Google Cloud services, Organization Policy gives enterprises the control they need to scale safely.

Explore the Organization Policy documentation to learn more about resource governance in Google Cloud and set up your foundational guardrails.

entries.content:
The Google Cloud Data Analytics, BI, and Database teams

Recent product news and updates from our data analytics, database and business intelligence teams.

November 9 - November 13

  • Bringing conversational analytics to Gemini with Data Cloud connectors: Data Cloud connectors in Gemini are now in preview, enabling knowledge workers to query live enterprise data using natural language directly within tools like Google Docs, Gmail, and Google Slides. The capability connects across BigQuery, Looker, Spanner, AlloyDB for PostgreSQL, and Cloud SQL without requiring data movement, grounded by Knowledge Catalog semantic models under user-identity IAM governance. Read the announcement blog.

  • Direct Apache Iceberg access in AlloyDB enables unified lakehouse querying: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL now supports direct querying of Apache Iceberg tables stored in Cloud Storage without requiring ETL pipelines or data duplication. Transactional applications can join operational data with analytical lakehouses in real time using standard PostgreSQL queries, accelerating cross-system analysis while maintaining complete relational integrity. Together with AlloyDB sync and lakehouse federation, you now have three integration approaches to choose from, depending on your use case. Read the launch blog.

  • AlloyDB Express delivers instant scale-to-zero PostgreSQL for developer prototyping: AlloyDB Express is now available, providing a lightweight, fast-provisioning PostgreSQL environment tailored for developers, testing, and AI coding agents like Antigravity. It scales to zero when idle to minimize costs while maintaining full PostgreSQL compatibility, allowing engineering teams to transition prototype workloads to production AlloyDB instances when ready. AlloyDB Express offers a free tier, with easy-to-understand pricing for higher usage. Read the announcement blog.

  • Carwow unifies its data foundation with BigQuery, Knowledge Catalog, and Looker to scale AI innovation: Europe's largest online car-changing marketplace migrated to BigQuery, Knowledge Catalog, and Looker to establish a governed single source of truth and enable trusted self-service analytics across the business. Paired with Gemini, Carwow automated vehicle document verification and PII redaction to save £2 million annually while cutting MLOps deployment cycles from months to weeks. Watch the Carwow customer story video.

  • Geospatial Analytics Playground enables natural-language exploration of BigQuery maps datasets: Google Maps Platform launched the Geospatial Analytics Playground, a natural-language evaluation environment built on top of Places Insights, Roads Management Insights, and Street View Insights datasets in BigQuery. Powered by Gemini, the open-source Agent Development Kit (ADK), and modular agent skills, the playground lets teams test spatial queries and validate dataset coverage without upfront spatial engineering. Read the announcement blog.

November 2 - November 6

  • BigQuery observability for data agents is now generally available: Data teams can now monitor the performance, adoption, latency, and cost of BigQuery data agents and their multi-turn conversations using Google Cloud Observability. This capability provides production-grade visibility into agent execution traces, usage volume, and query behavior so organizations can scale conversational analytics with confidence. Review the BigQuery release notes.

  • BigQuery change history and continuous queries for Apache Iceberg managed tables are now GA: BigQuery change history and continuous queries are now generally available for Lakehouse for Apache Iceberg managed tables. You can use the APPENDS table-valued function to track row additions over a specific time range and run continuous queries to read incoming data from and write output rows to Apache Iceberg managed tables. Review the BigQuery release notes.

  • BigQuery Data Engineering Agent adds support for BigQuery AI and ML functions: The BigQuery Data Engineering Agent now supports BigQuery AI, ML, and object functions and statements directly inside generated Dataform SQLX pipelines and agent instruction files. Paired with new folder-based Git repository integration in BigQuery Studio, data engineers can build, version, and automate AI-enriched data pipelines faster. Review the BigQuery release notes.

  • AlloyDB for PostgreSQL introduces AI-powered SQL tuning in preview: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL added the ai.tune_sql function in Public Preview. The function combines AI models with query execution plans and runtime statistics to automatically recommend query rewrites, missing indexes, vacuum operations, and database flag adjustments. Review the AlloyDB release notes.

  • Zero-downtime embedding model upgrades in AlloyDB AI: A new technical guide demonstrates how to upgrade vector embedding models in AlloyDB AI without disrupting production traffic. Using automatic embeddings alongside ScaNN vector indexes, engineering teams can transition to newer embedding models in the background while keeping semantic search and RAG applications online. Read the blog.

  • Shrink Cloud SQL for SQL Server storage disks with minimal downtime using Database Migration Service: A new technical guide demonstrates how to reclaim underutilized storage and reduce infrastructure costs on Cloud SQL for SQL Server instances using Database Migration Service (DMS). This workflow migrates databases to right-sized target disks with continuous replication so teams can downsize over-provisioned storage with minimal cutover downtime. Read the blog.

  • Dataflow Streaming Engine adds latency tiers and scheduled autoscaling: Dataflow introduced new horizontal autoscaling controls for Streaming Engine jobs, allowing teams to select low, medium, or high latency tiers to tune backlog sensitivity. Engineers can also configure recurring autoscaling schedules to adjust minimum and maximum worker counts or utilization targets during predictable traffic windows. Review the Dataflow release notes.

  • Spanner adds ON DELETE SET NULL foreign key actions across GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL: Spanner now supports the ON DELETE SET NULL referential action on foreign keys for both GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL dialects. When a referenced parent row is deleted, Spanner automatically updates the referencing child columns to NULL, simplifying schema migrations and relational integrity management. Review the Spanner release notes.

October 26 - October 30

  • LookML metadata indexing in Knowledge Catalog is now generally available: LookML models, Explores, Views, and join logic now continuously sync into the Knowledge Catalog context graph. This integration provides turnkey grounding for Gemini Enterprise and custom AI agents with deterministic business math, paired with end-to-end lineage tracing from underlying BigQuery tables directly to individual Looker dashboard tiles. Read the announcement blog.

  • Best Buy accelerates self-service insights with conversational analytics in BigQuery: Best Buy deployed conversational data agents directly against BigQuery to empower retail teams with multi-turn natural language exploration. The implementation reduces reliance on manual SQL and dedicated engineering queues, accelerating strategic planning and forecasting cycles while preserving enterprise governance and data protections validated against historical sales records. Explore the Best Buy customer story.

  • Myer accelerates retail insights with BigQuery data agents and Gemini: Leading department store Myer rolled out conversational data agents in BigQuery across 50+ retail analytics projects. Powered by Gemini, the solution enables commercial and merchandising teams to analyze store performance, stock levels, and customer trends using plain English, speeding up decision-making and reducing backlog requests for data teams. Read the Myer case study.

  • Rightmove speeds real estate analytics and predictive forecasting with Looker: The UK's top property portal unified its business analytics on Looker and BigQuery, delivering 4x faster reporting for 400+ team members and cutting meeting prep from hours to minutes. In addition, Rightmove built forecasting models that predict lead volume within 2–4.5% of actual results, while piloting Conversational Analytics in Looker. Read the Rightmove customer story.

  • BigQuery adds AI.TRANSLATE and AI.CHUNK_DOCUMENT for in-database text and RAG pipelines: BigQuery introduced two native generative AI capabilities to simplify unstructured data workflows directly within SQL. The 

    AI.TRANSLATE
    function enables multilingual translation across Neural Machine Translation and Translation LLMs, while the 
    AI.CHUNK_DOCUMENT
    table-valued function partitions unstructured text into semantically coherent segments optimized for vector embeddings and RAG pipelines. Review the BigQuery release notes.

  • AlloyDB adds in-database ai.extract and ai.classify functions to accelerate operational AI: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL introduced two new AI functions, 

    ai.extract
    and 
    ai.classify,
    in Public Preview, allowing developers to extract structured entities and categorize unstructured text directly inside SQL queries without external inference pipelines. These functions add to existing AlloyDB AI capabilities such as summarizing, generating, and filtering data with AI. Review the AlloyDB release notes.

  • AlloyDB Omni Web UI is generally available for centralized hybrid database management: The AlloyDB Omni Web UI is now generally available, providing a centralized graphical interface to manage hybrid and on-premises PostgreSQL deployments. Database administrators can monitor multi-cluster topologies, inspect columnar engine metrics, diagnose slow queries with Query Insights, and verify AI model connectivity across their database fleet. Review the AlloyDB Omni release notes.

  • Cloud Spanner adds approximate aggregate functions for high-speed analytics at scale: Cloud Spanner now supports approximate aggregate functions across both GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL dialects. Powered by HyperLogLog++ sketches, these functions generate fast statistical estimates for distinct count metrics with minimal compute overhead, accelerating analytical queries and reporting dashboards across petabyte-scale operational datasets. Review the Cloud Spanner release notes.

  • Knowledge Catalog introduces self-learning context enrichment and Knowledge Studio (Preview): Knowledge Catalog's enrichment agent now learns from agent and user interactions and from sources such as playbooks, code repositories, and business documents to find and fix missing or outdated context, which teams can package into reusable context sets. Knowledge Studio, the new studio experience in Knowledge Catalog, lets context engineers and data stewards explore their data estate conversationally, navigate a visual context graph, and review changes before they reach users and agents. Based on internal benchmarks, grounding agents in Knowledge Catalog makes them nearly 4x more accurate, with up to 33% lower latency and using up to 75% fewer tokens. Read the launch blog.

  • Knowledge Catalog now grounds AI agents in the semantic models you already trust (GA): Knowledge Catalog natively ingests semantic models and metric definitions from Looker LookML, BigQuery Graph, dbt MetricFlow, Snowflake Semantic Views, Databricks Metric Views, and SAP Core Schema Notation, and connects them with lineage, data quality, and access controls in a single context graph. Gemini Enterprise, BigQuery conversational analytics, and custom agents retrieve a metric's trusted formula, verified join path, and backing table in one context call, without moving data or rewriting business logic. Read the launch blog.

October 19 - October 23

  • BigQuery introduces column aliases in GoogleSQL and cross-region table copy GA

    GoogleSQL in BigQuery now supports column aliases in 

    SELECT
    and 
    WHERE
    clauses (GA opt-in), avoiding nested subqueries and simplifying migrations from Snowflake and Teradata. Cross-region table copying is also now generally available to streamline regional data replication and disaster recovery. Review the BigQuery release notes.

  • Conversational analytics in BigQuery expands to Canada and adds CSV/PDF export

    Conversational analytics in BigQuery is now available in Montréal (

    northamerica-northeast1
    ) and Toronto (
    northamerica-northeast2
    ) to support Canadian data residency requirements. You can also now export agent responses — including text, tables, charts, and citations — directly to CSV or PDF (GA). Learn more about conversational analytics in BigQuery.

  • AlloyDB Omni 18.4.0 is now GA with Advanced Query Insights and external KMS support

    AlloyDB Omni 18.4.0 brings PostgreSQL 18.4 to self-hosted and multi-cloud environments, adding the 

    google_insights_v2
    extension for granular query execution and wait-event diagnostics. It also adds Thales CipherTrust Manager support for Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) alongside HashiCorp Vault. Explore the AlloyDB Omni release notes.

  • Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL adds managed connection pooling and Private Service Connect defaults

    Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL now supports enabling built-in managed connection pooling on existing Private Service Connect (PSC) instances to scale high-concurrency workloads. PSC is also now the default private IP option for new Cloud SQL instances in new projects to simplify cross-project networking. Review Cloud SQL updates.

  • Customer momentum: Unico prevents over $5B in fraud on Google's Agentic Data Cloud

    Digital identity platform Unico migrated from Databricks Spark/Scala clusters to BigQuery and Spanner at the core of its data architecture. Unifying real-time transaction streams with petabyte-scale analytics enabled low-latency identity verification that has prevented over $5 billion in fraud. Read the Unico case study.

  • Developer guide: Getting started with Looker Data Apps

    Following the debut of Looker Data Apps in preview, a new walkthrough on the Google Developer Community shares practical patterns for building prompt-driven applications inside Looker. Read the guide on the Google Developer Community.

October 12 - October 16

  • Looker Data Apps are now in Preview to build and host interactive, agent-generated applications natively inside Looker

    Generated using natural language prompts, the Antigravity CLI, or Claude Code, these interactive web applications, natively hosted inside Looker, transform business reporting into operational systems of action. Users can test scenarios, adjust parameters, and trigger workflows in downstream platforms while inheriting LookML semantic modeling, row-level security, and access controls with no runtime LLM token costs. Read the announcement blog.

  • Build end-to-end data science pipelines with the Data Agent Kit

    Following the general availability of the Data Agent Kit, a new end-to-end walkthrough demonstrates how data teams can build, test, and schedule machine learning pipelines directly from their preferred code editors. Explore the walkthrough and codelab.

  • Manage dashboard agents as code to bring CI/CD and version control to LookML dashboards

    Data teams can now declare agent parameters, configurations, and prompt instructions alongside dashboard files in code. This integration enables standard developer workflows for conversational BI, including Git version control, peer review, branching, and automated CI/CD validation before agent modifications reach production end users. Read the technical guide on the Google Developer Community.

  • Simplify AI search with native AlloyDB hybrid search and Reciprocal Rank Fusion

    AlloyDB for PostgreSQL simplifies hybrid search architectures by combining vector similarity search and keyword BM25 retrieval within a unified database engine. Using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), developers can merge lexical scoring and semantic embeddings into a single ranked result without writing a complex SQL query. This unified approach removes the operational overhead of running and synchronizing external search engines alongside operational databases for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and search applications.Explore hybrid search in AlloyDB.

October 5 - October 9

  • Data Agent Kit is now generally available to bring Google Data Cloud to any coding agent

    Data Agent Kit provides a free collection of Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools and Google-authored agent skills that connect more than 15 Google Data Cloud services directly to coding agents across VS Code, Antigravity, Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex. This release expands support for developers and data practitioners to inspect schemas, author queries, and build end-to-end data pipelines in natural language directly from their IDE or CLI. Read the announcement blog.

  • Spanner Omni is now generally available for deploy-anywhere, multi-model workloads

    Spanner Omni brings Spanner's distributed SQL, graph, vector, and key-value capabilities to any environment, including on-premises data centers, other public clouds via Kubernetes or VMs, and local developer laptops. Organizations can build and run multi-model applications with consistent APIs and query engines across hybrid and multi-cloud footprints while seamlessly scaling to managed Spanner on Google Cloud. Read the launch blog and explore how Spanner also removed cumulative mutation limits for DML transactions.

  • AlloyDB delivers PostgreSQL for agents and native BM25 hybrid search

    We announced PostgreSQL for agents in AlloyDB, introducing an agentic database architecture engineered for real-time data access at agent scale with workload isolation. In addition, native BM25 ranking is now in Preview for AlloyDB and Cloud SQL, allowing developers to combine keyword search and vector embeddings directly in PostgreSQL without maintaining an external search engine. For hybrid deployments, the AlloyDB Omni RPM Orchestrator is now generally available, and you can dive deeper in our new Build AI apps and agents with AlloyDB eBook.

  • Lakehouse runtime catalog adds regional endpoints across 22 regions and GA support for flexible column names

    Lakehouse runtime catalog regional endpoints are now live across 22 Google Cloud regions across the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and the Middle East, supporting both the Apache Iceberg REST catalog endpoint and the Apache Hive catalog endpoint to help customers meet strict data residency and sovereignty requirements. In addition, flexible column names for Apache Iceberg tables are now generally available by default across Iceberg external tables and managed tables, enabling seamless querying of columns containing spaces, hyphens, and Unicode characters. We also announced the Preview of cross-cloud caching and connections for the borderless Lakehouse.

  • Unlock predictive and agent-ready insights with BigQuery augmented analytics TVFs, TabFM, and identity columns

    BigQuery introduced augmented analytics table-valued functions (TVFs): six built-in functions that automate metric diagnostics, trend analysis, and pattern discovery directly where your data lives and integrate as skills for AI agents. We also introduced TabFM in BigQuery to bring tabular foundation model capabilities to predictive analytics, alongside BigQuery identity columns to automatically generate sequential surrogate keys and simplify data warehouse pipelines.

  • Dataflow adds Pause/Resume and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU support for large-scale AI workloads

    New Dataflow capabilities make it easier to run high-throughput streaming and batch AI pipelines at scale, including Pause/Resume job controls and support for NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs. And for teams running Apache Spark workloads, learn how to mitigate compute stockouts and maximize availability using flexible VMs.

  • Unlock up to 3x higher QPS and microsecond latency with Memorystore for Valkey 9.1

    Memorystore for Valkey 9.1 is now available, delivering up to 3x higher queries per second (QPS) and microsecond-level caching latencies to accelerate high-throughput applications and real-time AI agent state management. Read the blog.

  • Customer momentum across Google Data Cloud — Yahoo, PayPal, Surescripts, Airwallex, and Lucius AI

    Organizations across industries are scaling their data and AI foundations on Google Data Cloud. Yahoo uses flexible VMs in Managed Service for Apache Spark to reduce provisioning failures by 85%, while PayPal migrated mission-critical analytics workloads to Managed Service for Apache Spark to scale and reduce operational overhead. On the database front, Surescripts migrated 30.5 billion annual healthcare transactions to AlloyDB with 99.998% uptime, Airwallex manages more than 5,000 databases with 99.99% availability on Cloud SQL with a team of four DBAs, and Lucius AI runs a 210,000-tender global platform on AlloyDB and MCP with 47x faster ScaNN vector search.

September 7 - September 10

  • Pub/Sub SMTs can now AI Inference your Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform models!

    Pub/Sub AI Inference SMTs allow you to apply inference on an incoming stream of events using models hosted in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. The model’s prediction is appended to your event, making it available for downstream processing in your data warehouse (like BigQuery) or operational database (like BigTable). This feature, now generally available, can dramatically simplify or enhance anomaly detection systems you are operating. 

  • PostgreSQL Source Connector is now generally available in Managed Service for Apache Kafka!

    Managed Service for Apache Kafka’s PostgreSQL connector allows customers to capture changes from their PostgreSQL database and ingest them into their Kafka infrastructure with low latency. This source connector is compatible withCloud SQL for Postgres, AlloyDB, and self-managed PostgreSQL databases. Try this along with our entire portfolio of managed connectors, including MirrorMaker 2.0, BigQuery, Cloud Storage, and Pub/Sub! E-mail kafka-hotline@google.com if you have questions or feedback!

  • Pause-on-failure for Dataflow batch jobs is GA

    Dataflow pause-on-failure enables you to preserve the state of a batch Dataflow job before it fails. By pausing your Dataflow job, you can address issues that are external to the pipeline and resume processing without losing completed work. This helps you better manage resource costs and improve job reliability when you face temporary outages or capacity constraints.

  • The insertAll API is now the BigQuery Storage Write API (REST)

    The legacy insertAll streaming API is now rebranded as the BigQuery Storage Write API (REST). By dropping the "legacy" label, developers can confidently build long-term HTTP-based streaming workflows. This stateless JSON-over-HTTPS endpoint offers a lightweight alternative to heavy gRPC libraries—ideal for serverless web apps, IoT telemetry, and AI logging. The transition is seamless for existing users, requiring zero code changes and offering 100% backward compatibility. However, the Storage Write API (gRPC) version remains the recommended standard for high-throughput, continuous pipelines.

August 31 - September 4

  • Stateful processing is available in BigQuery continuous queries in Preview

    Stateful operations significantly expand what’s possible with BigQuery continuous queries. This feature allows users to leverage functions like 
    JOIN
    s, aggregations, and windowing functions directly in their streaming queries. Now you can calculate metrics over time (for example, a 30-minute average) to power your downstream applications and AI agents with much richer, real-time signals.

    Try out our featurehere and share your feedback with bq-continuous-queries-feedback@google.com!

  • Synthetic data generator tool is available for Managed Service for Kafka

    You’ve launched your first Kafka cluster. Now what? The next thing to do is to produce some data to the cluster, but that involves modifying a client application somewhere or spinning up a virtual machine. The synthetic data generator tool, now generally available, can start sending mock data to your cluster in 3 clicks, and will get data streaming into your cluster in less than two minutes. The perfect utility for those moments you just want to test your cluster and new features. Try our quickstart today!

  • Dataflow pipeline updates are faster & more flexible

    Dataflow pipeline updates can now stop-and-replace pipelines, a major addition to the existing in-place-update feature. The new parallel pipeline option accelerates the migration between the old & new pipeline, resulting in reduced disruption to your business. You can also set a timeout on drains that prevents runaway costs for your pipeliness in the event of stuck processing. This feature is generally available. Try it here!

July 6 - July 10

  • New Lakehouse managed tables now in preview

    Lakehouse tables for Apache Iceberg are now in preview and available in the console. By using Google-managed Apache Iceberg tables in Lakehouse, you can eliminate the overhead of maintaining duplicate data pipelines and complex synchronization logic between BigQuery and open-source engines. This unified table format delivers native, multi-engine read and write interoperability, allowing you to run concurrent DML/DDL operations across diverse analytics tools on a single, shared storage layer.  Built-in automated table management handles painful background optimization tasks like compaction and partition tuning, freeing up your team to focus on building rather than managing storage maintenance.

This series is designed for a broad audience: whether you are exploring these databases for the first time or are an existing user looking to leverage the new capabilities announced at Next '26.

Look out for more locations coming soon

With no credit card required to start, you can easily ingest workloads and manage workloads that require low-latency, high-throughput, and predictable access. Plus, new Google Cloud customers get $300 in free credits on signup.

May 11 - May 15

April 20 - April 24

    We are excited to announce the launch of the new, Google-built ODBC driver for BigQuery. This new open-source driver provides a direct, high-performance connection for applications to BigQuery and is developed entirely in-house by Google.Download a new driver and connect your application to BigQuery.

This announcement extends the ability for AI models to plan, build, and solve complex problems, connecting to the database tools our customers leverage daily as the backbone of their work environment.

  • We outlined how you can build a conversational agent in BigQuery using the Conversational Analytics API to help you build context-aware agents that can understand natural language, query your BigQuery data, and deliver answers in text, tables, and visual charts.

February 16 - February 20

Companies like Arrive, Audika, Carousell, Framebridge, GumGum, Intel, Overdose Digital, Ocean Network Express, Subskribe and Promevo are leveraging Looker’s newest AI-driven capabilities, including Conversational Analytics, to transform data to insights and actions, and empower their entire organization with a single source of truth, powered by Looker’s semantic layer.

February 2 - February 6

  • Join us on March 4 for our webinar, Win Your AI Strategy with Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus, to learn how to power your generative AI workloads with 3x higher performance and 99.99% availability. Register today to discover how to build a scalable, enterprise-grade foundation for your most demanding AI applications.

January 26 - January 30

  • We introduced Conversational Analytics in BigQuery, which allows users to analyze data using natural language.   • We outlined how data products have become the foundation for AI agents, providing the context needed to make autonomous agents reliable and trusted for real business use, backed by organized business logic and semantic understanding.
  • We highlighted how you can supercharge data analytics workflows, and outlined Google Cloud’s AI agent offerings for data engineering, data science, and development tools, so you can integrate agentic workflows in your applications, empower your teams and speed discovery.

January 19 - January 23

Experience a powerful new engine featuring over a hundred new query features, index-less queries, new index types, and observability tooling to improve query performance. Seamlessly migrate using built-in tools and leverage Firestore’s existing differentiated serverless foundation, virtually unlimited scale, and industry-leading SLA. January 12 - January 16

This new open-source driver provides a direct, high-performance connection for Java applications to BigQuery and is developed entirely in-house by Google.Download a new driver and connect your Java application to BigQuery.

Gemini analyzes logs and task metadata to identify failure patterns—such as resource exhaustion or timeouts—and provides actionable recommendations driven by Gemini Cloud Assist to resolve the issue. This integration shifts the debugging experience from manual toil to automated root cause analysis, significantly reducing the time required to restore your pipelines. entries.content:
Andre Alfred

Sr. Director, Cloud Security Threat Operations

Modern security operations centers (SOCs) face an ongoing pipeline dilemma. While ingesting comprehensive endpoint telemetry is non-negotiable for defense, conventional delivery paths often drive up transfer overhead and alert latency. As attackers operate at machine speed, any unnecessary friction in how data moves from endpoints to the SOC can leave teams without the insight they need to respond to attacks in real time.

Addressing this requires optimizing the data pipeline at the integration layer. Rather than routing telemetry through complex intermediary cloud buckets that require ongoing maintenance and introduce costly processing delays, engineering teams need a streamlined delivery architecture. By eliminating architectural bottlenecks and optimizing data transit, security operations and IT leaders can significantly compress ingest latency, lower operational overhead, and give analysts near-instant visibility where it matters most.

Google Cloud and SentinelOne collaborated to solve this scaling challenge with a fundamentally re-architected integration. As a Google Unified Security Recommended endpoint detection and response (EDR) partner, SentinelOne pairs with Google Security Operations through direct integration and streamlined data schemas, delivering essential endpoint telemetry visibility to Google Security Operations detection and agentic SOC pipelines while significantly reducing the total cost of ownership of the integration.

What’s at stake?

For enterprise customers, every minute of telemetry latency can increase the blast radius of an active intrusion. When detection pipelines take half an hour to surface adversary activity, incident response transitions from active mitigation to retrospective damage control.

For the broader security community and IT leadership, inefficient ingestion pipelines can impact budget and compute resources. Retaining bulky, unoptimized telemetry in intermediate staging environments diverts resources away from strategic security initiatives and saddles engineering teams with unneeded infrastructure debt.

Technical highlights and capabilities

The re-engineered integration between Google Cloud and SentinelOne introduces six dedicated engineering workstreams designed to remove ingestion bottlenecks and reduce data overhead without sacrificing detection fidelity:

  • Significant event size reduction: A modernized EDR data schema greatly reduces the average event size, preserving full analytical fidelity and reducing downstream compute load for agentic workflows.

  • Direct Google API ingestion: SentinelOne directly streams events into Google Security Operations with APIs, eliminating intermediate cloud storage hops and associated storage fees.

  • Reduced streaming latency: Removing the requirement for intermediate cloud storage makes data available for detection, investigative, and agentic workflows in Google Security Operations in near real-time.

  • Precision telemetry scoping: Integrated SentinelOne Cloud Funnel filters allow further flexibility to customize telemetry sent to Google Security Operations.

  • Unified alerts API and Mandiant alignment: Parsers, alert models, and SOAR playbooks were engineered alongside Mandiant Incident Response and Managed Defense teams to support automated host isolation, full-disk deep visibility scans, malware extraction, and artifact enrichment directly from Google Security Operations.

  • Industry-validated partnership: Named Google Threat Intelligence's Intel Partner of the Year at Google Cloud Next.

Transform your SOC ingestion today

Modern defense requires direct action, not delayed transit. By cutting out unnecessary staging layers and streaming directly via APIs, your security team gains the speed needed to outpace modern threats while protecting your budget.

Targeted for phased delivery by end of year, initial rollouts are prioritizing customers using Mandiant Managed Defense and Mandiant Threat Defense. Contact your Google Cloud or SentinelOne account team today to evaluate your current telemetry pipeline, schedule a technical architecture review, and reserve early access for your environment.
